title: Case Study 00521 – 17 April 2026 – 30 Questions a Hypnotherapist might ask to Customize a Healing Program for you to address your Pornography addiction using Hypnotherapy.
description: Case Study 00521 – 17 April 2026 30 Questions to Customize Your Hypnotherapy Healing Program for Pornography Addiction These questions are designed to identify
h1: Case Study 00521 – 17 April 2026 – 30 Questions a Hypnotherapist might ask to Customize a Healing Program for you to address your Pornography addiction using Hypnotherapy.

h3Items.h3: 30 Questions to Customize Your Hypnotherapy Healing Program for Pornography Addiction

bullets: When did you first begin using pornography regularly?
How often do you currently engage with it?
What times of day are most common for use?
What role does pornography play in your daily or weekly routine?
What do you believe it provides for you (e.g., relief, escape, stimulation)?
What situations or environments most often trigger the urge?
Are there specific emotional states that lead to use?
Do certain times (late at night, alone time) increase temptation?
What typically happens right before you engage in it?
What thoughts or justifications arise in that moment?
What feelings are you trying to create or avoid?
Do you use pornography to cope with stress, anxiety, loneliness, or boredom?
How do you feel immediately before, during, and after use?
Are there unresolved emotional experiences linked to this behavior?
What emotions feel hardest to sit with without turning to pornography?
Do you feel in control of your behavior? Why or why not?
Have you tried to stop or reduce before? What happened?
What typically leads to relapse or continued use?
What routines or habits reinforce the behavior?
How automatic does this behavior feel (habit vs conscious choice)?
What beliefs do you hold about pornography and its impact on your life?
How do you currently see yourself in relation to this behavior?
What identity would you prefer to have instead?
Do you believe you can change? Why or why not?
What limiting beliefs might be holding you back?
How has this behavior affected your relationships, focus, or productivity?
What areas of your life have been negatively impacted?
What improvements would you expect if you stopped or reduced?
How does this behavior affect your motivation and performance?
What would your ideal life look like without this pattern?

paragraphs: This intake allows the hypnotherapist to:
bullets: Identify subconscious triggers and reward associations
Address emotional regulation strategies
Interrupt habitual loops and automatic behaviors
Reframe beliefs and reduce shame-based thinking
Build a new identity aligned with control, clarity, and purpose

paragraphs: Compulsive pornography use is often driven by:
bullets: Dopamine-based reward conditioning
Emotional avoidance or self-soothing patterns
Habit loops tied to environment and routine

registry.seoTitle: 30 Hypnotherapy Intake Questions for Alcohol Addiction
registry.seoDescription: Thirty intake questions a hypnotherapist may use to customise alcohol addiction healing programme support.

title: Case Study 00931 – 20 March 2026 – 30 Questions a Hypnotherapist might ask to Customize a Healing Program for you to address your Alcohol addiction (Alcohol Use Disorder) using Hypnotherapy.
description: Case Study 00931 – 20 March 2026 30 Questions to Customize Your Hypnotherapy Healing Program These questions are designed to uncover patterns, triggers, beliefs
h1: Case Study 00931 – 20 March 2026 – 30 Questions a Hypnotherapist might ask to Customize a Healing Program for you to address your Alcohol addiction (Alcohol Use Disorder) using Hypnotherapy.

h3Items.h3: 30 Questions to Customize Your Hypnotherapy Healing Program
h3Items.body: These questions are designed to uncover patterns, triggers, beliefs, and emotional drivers behind alcohol use, allowing for a deeply individualized hypnotherapy approach.

bullets: When did you first start drinking regularly?
How would you describe your current drinking pattern?
What role does alcohol play in your daily or weekly life?
When do you feel the strongest urge to drink?
What do you believe alcohol gives you that you need?
What emotions most often lead you to drink?
Are there specific situations or environments that trigger your drinking?
How do you usually feel just before you take a drink?
What thoughts go through your mind when you crave alcohol?
Are there recurring stressors or unresolved issues linked to your drinking?
Have you noticed any patterns (time, place, people) associated with drinking?
What habits or routines are connected to alcohol use?
What happens after you start drinking—can you stop easily?
Have you tried to cut down or stop before? What happened?
What typically causes relapse or loss of control?
How do you currently cope with stress, anxiety, or discomfort?
Do you experience feelings of guilt, shame, or regret related to drinking?
What beliefs do you hold about yourself and your ability to change?
Are there past experiences or traumas that may influence your behavior?
How would you describe your overall mental and emotional wellbeing?
How do you see yourself right now?
How would you like to see yourself in the future?
Do you identify as someone who struggles with alcohol, or something else?
What kind of person do you believe you are when you are not drinking?
What personal strengths can support your recovery?
Why do you want to change your relationship with alcohol now?
What would success look like for you (complete abstinence, moderation, control)?
What are the biggest benefits you expect from stopping or reducing drinking?
What fears or concerns do you have about quitting?
What kind of support or changes would make this journey easier for you?

sections.h2: How These Questions Help in Hypnotherapy
paragraphs: These questions allow the hypnotherapist to:
bullets: Identify subconscious triggers and conditioned responses
Reframe limiting beliefs about alcohol and self-control
Build personalized hypnotic suggestions and scripts
Address emotional root causes rather than just symptoms
Strengthen motivation and future identity
